title: A Design-Based Approach to Testing and Inference in (Quasi-)Experiments with Spillovers
abstract: arXiv:2607.08640v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Economic policies rarely affect only their direct targets. To study these spillovers, researchers summarize who else was treated with a simple exposure measure, such as the share of treated neighbors within a radius. But for many settings, economic theory provides little guidance on choosing the functional form (e.g., ring) of that measure or its parameters (e.g., radius). We show that the data can inform both choices. Correctly specified exposure measures imply orthogonality conditions that can be used for both estimation and testing. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimator under spatial and network dependence in a design-based framework, with all randomness arising from treatment assignment. We then characterize the efficient moment conditions. Applied to two large-scale anti-poverty programs, the framework supports some prior radius estimates but rejects others. tldr: 本文提出一种基于设计的方法，利用数据来选择和检验溢出效应中的暴露度量形式及其参数，并通过正交性条件实现有效估计和推断。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a design-based approach that uses data to select and test the functional form and parameters of exposure measures in spillover settings, enabling efficient estimation and inference via orthogonality conditions.
